newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa trims losses in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa trims losses in featureless trade.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended weaker but off session lows as the market managed to gather some support despite a meagre turnover.
Origin selling and trade liquidation kept prices under pressure but Tuesday's relatively small losses suggested that nearby support could be working.

Traders noted reports that Ghana's purchases in the fifth week ending November 14 totalled 22,432 tonnes compared with 28,428 tonnes in the corresponding week of the previous season. But there was no price reaction.
Prices also failed to move on news that General Cocoa "guesstimated" Ivorian arrivals by November 30 at around 290,000 tonnes compared with an estimated total of 410,000 in the same period last year.
"His report was in the market since Friday," commented one trader. "I don't think it had any impact."
Benchmark March cocoa finished dealings down three stg on the day at 931 stg a tonne after a low of 924 which traders now consider as immediate support. Wider support is seen at 920.
Other contracts were narrowly mixed and volume totalled 2,786 lots, almost half of which were crosses and AAs.
In their weekly newsletter General Cocoa also estimated total Ivorian sales of the 1996/97 crop at 775,000 tonnes and 1997/98 sales at 100,000 tonnes.
